The scope call round 2 parked for Thomas — is the Inter-Departmental Business Register a publication or something else? — answers itself against corpus precedent: statcan-business-register, nl-cbs-sbr and it-istat-asia-enterprises are all statistical business registers already carried as kind 'publication', so gb-ons-idbr is minted the same way. That decision is what makes ASHE and BRES worth having: BRES's only real dependency is the IDBR sampling frame, and without the register it would have arrived on a Code-of-Practice compliance edge alone. Two findings changed the shape of this round. The predicted CPI edge landed at A but not on the artefact expected: CPIH's owner-occupier component is sourced from the Price Index of Private Rents, not the UK House Price Index — ONS explicitly rules house prices OUT of CPIH in the same methodology article, which is a documented negative rather than a silence. And ASHE's sampling frame is PAYE, not the IDBR; the IDBR enters afterwards to match employer contact details onto the drawn sample. reports.title: Inter-Departmental Business Register
reports.description: The comprehensive list of UK businesses used across government for statistical purposes, and the main sampling frame for business surveys run by ONS and other departments. Its two main inputs are VAT and PAYE records from HMRC, supplemented by Companies House, Dun and Bradstreet and ONS business surveys; it covers around 2.7 million businesses, and because the two tax sources have thresholds, very small businesses below them are generally not included. ONS states it is fully compliant with EC Regulation No 177/2008 on the harmonisation of business registers for statistical purposes.
reports.cadence_note: A continuously maintained register rather than a periodic release; releases_per_year is nominal, so that its absence would keep meaning 'one-off' (types.ts). ONS publishes from it annually — 'UK Business: Activity, Size and Location' and 'Business Demography' — alongside a data analysis service and a disclosive-microdata route through the Microdata Release Panel.

reports.title: Price Paid Data
reports.description: HM Land Registry's dataset of all property sales in England and Wales sold for value and lodged for registration, published in text and CSV form under the Open Government Licence and updated on the 20th working day of each month. It carries address data processed against Ordnance Survey's AddressBase Premium, and is the price source the UK House Price Index is built from.
reports.cadence_note: HM Land Registry: 'We update the data on the 20th working day of each month.'

reports.title: UK House Price Index
reports.description: The monthly index of residential property price change for the UK, produced from administrative land-registration records rather than a survey and published by HM Land Registry on behalf of a joint production with Registers of Scotland, Land & Property Services Northern Ireland and ONS. It combines price data with property-attribute data in a hedonic regression model, with the attributes for England and Wales taken from the Valuation Office Agency's Council Tax Valuation List. Data run from 1995 for England and Wales, 2004 for Scotland and 2005 for Northern Ireland. ONS places house prices outside the scope of consumer price inflation, so this index is not a CPIH input.

reports.title: Price Index of Private Rents
reports.description: The monthly measure of private rental price inflation across the whole privately rented stock, new and existing tenancies, published in the 'Private rent and house prices, UK' bulletin from March 2024 and extended to the whole UK from March 2025. It replaced the Index of Private Housing Rental Prices, ONS's lead measure of rental price change before that. It is built from administrative rental data collected by Rent Officers at the HMRC Valuation Office, the Scottish and Welsh Governments and the Northern Ireland Housing Executive, and the same rental data construct the owner-occupiers' housing costs component of CPIH under the rental equivalence approach.
title_aliases: Index of Private Housing Rental Prices

reports.title: Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings
reports.description: The annual survey of the levels, distribution and make-up of employee earnings and paid hours in the UK, published as the 'Employee earnings in the UK' bulletin. It is based on a 1% random sample of employee jobs drawn from HMRC Pay As You Earn records, with employers supplying the earnings and hours information; the drawn sample is matched against the Inter-Departmental Business Register for employer contact details, and returned data are weighted to UK population totals from the Labour Force Survey. It does not cover the self-employed or employees not paid in the reference period.

reports.title: Business Register and Employment Survey
reports.description: The annual business survey giving employee and employment estimates at detailed industrial and geographical levels, which ONS regards as the definitive source of official employee statistics by industry. Its sample of roughly 87,000 businesses is drawn from the Inter-Departmental Business Register, stratified by SIC 2007, country and register employment size; NISRA collects the same information independently in Northern Ireland and the two are combined for UK estimates. BRES results are also fed back to update the employment data held on the IDBR.

_dropped.why: REFUSED 2026-09-06 — the document says the opposite, and this is the round's most useful negative. ONS's CPIH housing methodology page explicitly excludes house prices from CPIH: 'OOH measures do not seek to capture increases in house prices. The inclusion of an asset price and therefore capital gains are generally defined as being out of scope of any kind of consumer price index. ... Property price changes are instead measured in the UK House Price Index.' The only documented CPIH-family use of UK HPI is in the net acquisitions index, discontinued from March 2020 — a different publication. The CPI bulletin names the UK HPI only in its 'Related links' block, which is navigation, not sourcing. The real CPI source edge is to the Price Index of Private Rents, minted this round.

NEAR MISS 2026-09-06, flagged rather than forced. The PIPR QMI's Table 1 has a column headed 'Valuation Office Council Tax' with note 1 reading 'The linking rate to HM Revenue and Customs Valuation Office Council Tax has increased over time...'. Under the 2026-09-06 ruling a methodology table cell naming a source counts, so the shape qualifies — but the string is 'Valuation Office Council Tax', not the artefact title 'Council Tax Valuation List', so the agency-not-artefact rule was applied strictly. PIPR's own rental data come from VOA Rent Officers administering Housing Benefit and Universal Credit, a different VOA function from the rating and council tax valuation lists. Wants a sentence naming the list.
